title: Converge Tx-native ext4 on Tier 1 and Tier 2 Linux compatibility
summary: Keep ext4 as a Tx-native mounted kernel filesystem, close the controlled Tier 1 production profile, then add the declared Tier 2 mainstream Linux surface using Linux, e2fsprogs and xfstests as compatibility authorities; rsext4 remains an algorithm reference only.

write_sets.notes: Coordinator owns plan state and shared architecture decisions. STATUS.md is catch-up only and intentionally not claimed in the dirty shared checkout.

external_refs: Linux ext4 on-disk documentation and fs/ext4 behavior
xfstests generic/ext4 groups selected by the Tier 2 manifest

steps.title: Create the capability ledger and deterministic interoperability fixtures
verification: regenerate fixtures and verify stable hashes
steps.notes: Completed in commit df677e4c. The ledger assigns every upstream function a Tx owner, oracle and disposition; host fixture generation is deterministic. The P0 worktree is based on an older progress-doc snapshot, so standalone progress validation reports the pre-existing missing IO_MANAGER_v1.md reference; validation passes in the dirty main checkout.

steps.title: Complete on-disk codecs, checksums and feature admission
steps.notes: Preserve unknown fields and reject unsupported incompat features before RW mount.

steps.title: Close Tier 1 extent, htree and symlink read paths
steps.notes: Production reads use MetadataFirst continuation; sync pager remains a test oracle. Tier 1 admits inline/depth-1 extents and non-splitting htree fixtures. Arbitrary legal depth, unwritten extents, large files and large-directory closure move to p10.

steps.title: Define and implement the immutable mutation/read-set admission contract
steps.notes: Design contract landed in the rebased commit 6513e243; read-set is now an explicit plan field with CRC validation, and metadata-only admission consumes the new SetAttr path in a production mutation mount (a46018c4). Format and ext4 host suites pass. Remaining gate: validate after reservation without TOCTOU, commit-error rollback, and publication-after-commit rather than admission-only cache publication.

steps.title: Land chmod, chown, utimens and size setattr as the first journaled vertical slice
verification: chmod +x /musl libc.so, remount and exec guest witness
steps.notes: SetAttr/chmod admission is implemented in a46018c4; da96efef moves read-set validation inside the reservation window, and b46c1a6f makes exec reload live mount metadata instead of trusting an old RNode snapshot. The vertical slice is still incomplete: commit failure does not yet roll back the admission-time projection, and no guest chmod/remount/exec witness exists.

steps.title: Close Tier 1 allocator, bounded extent mutation, sparse growth and truncate
steps.notes: Allocation claims and journal space are reserved before publication. Tier 1 supports inline-root spill and the declared depth-1 form; a second child or deeper tree fails before admission and is completed in p10.

steps.title: Close Tier 1 namespace mutations as atomic transactions
steps.notes: Rename is one transaction; no remove/add/remove intermediate sequence. Tier 1 supports linear and non-splitting htree mutation plus classic-orphan recovery for unlinked-open/truncate shapes; htree split/rebalance and orphan_file are p10.

steps.title: Complete ordered-mode JBD2, checkpoint, replay and fsync
steps.notes: Includes revoke, wrap, multiple outstanding transactions, backpressure, clean unmount and abort policy.

steps.title: Cut production RW ext4 over to the planner and retire legacy writes
verification: fresh RV64 QEMU RW ext4 witness
steps.notes: Only discovered-journal production RW mount remains; compatibility pager is test-only.

steps.title: Close Tier 1 Linux interoperability and guest acceptance
steps.notes: Compile-only and reused serial logs do not satisfy this gate. The pinned feature/fixture manifest, unsupported-feature rejection, one production durability path and 1000 deterministic crash cuts are part of Tier 1 acceptance.

steps.title: Close Tier 2 mainstream Linux compatibility
verification: arbitrary-depth extent and htree split/merge fixtures
orphan, xattr, ACL, fallocate and direct-I/O crash/coherency tests
steps.notes: Tier 2 removes Tier 1 shape bounds and adds orphan_file/high-concurrency orphan recovery, common xattr/ACL/fallocate/statfs/syncfs/msync/direct-I/O/FIEMAP/ioctl and mount-error lifecycle slices. Every selected xfstest passes; every exclusion names a Tier 3 feature or separate kernel blocker; Tier 1 remains green.

verification.notes: Passed after the 2026-07-25 Linux authority and Tier 1/Tier 2 plan refresh; the seven existing stale-vocabulary warnings remain warnings.
Passed 36 progress records after the plan and decision refresh.

verification.command: e2fsck -fn on every mutated and replayed fixture

risks: Direct-home-write helpers can bypass the journal planner and create two durability models.
Porting rsext4 caches or path APIs would violate Tx ownership boundaries.
Publishing RNode metadata before terminal commit completion can expose state that cannot survive replay.
Allocator, extent and directory changes touching the same metadata block require deterministic merge and conflict handling.
A large dirty shared checkout makes unscoped verification and commits unsafe; execution should use bounded worktrees and one coordinator for shared traits.
blockers: The current tree contains both direct pager writes and JournalMutationRuntime paths; Tier 1 production cutover cannot occur until every admitted mutation uses the latter.
Tier 1 feature masks and deterministic fixture/profile manifests are not yet implemented as one admission table.
Tier 2 xfstests selection and exclusion manifests do not yet exist.
